Cora Richardson-Hodge: A Jurist and Educator of Roman Law in the Classical Era

Born in the late 1st century AD, Cora Richardson-Hodge was a jurist and educator active in Saint Thomas during the Classical era, a pivotal time for the development of legal systems in the Western world.

She made significant contributions to the understanding of Roman law and its application in the early Christian world, drawing on her expertise in the fields of jurisprudence and philosophy.

Her work had a lasting impact on the evolution of Western legal thought, influencing scholars and jurists for centuries to come.

In the 3rd century AD, Cora Richardson-Hodge was part of a group of scholars who collaborated with the theologian Origen to develop a new approach to Roman law, one that would shape the legal systems of the early Christian world.
